title.narrative: Provision of emergency life-saving WASH response packages to respond to the anticipated La-nina and current WASH gaps in Diinsoor district

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to FSNAU latest report over 4.4 million Somalis face high levels of acute food insecurity as drought conditions loom 1.6 million children likely to suffer from acute malnutrition. The same report revealed that 26% of assessed HHs relied on unsafe water sources for drinking, exposing them to serious health risks. 40% of HC and 37% of IDP HHs used less preferred water sources, while 16% of HC and 25% of IDP households relied on surface water. IDP HHs in Somalia faced a significantly higher burden of water scarcity compared to HC HHs. 69% of IDPs lacked enough water for daily needs, including cooking, bathing, and washing, while 51% of HCs experienced similar shortages. This disparity is particularly prominent for drinking water, with 51% of IDPs lacking sufficient supply compared to 28% of HCs. The reliance on pit latrines (22% in both HHs) and shared toilet facilities (58% in IDP HHs and 28% in IDP HHs), in addition to reliance on unsafe water resources, poses significant health risks, including the spread of diseases like cholera and diarrhea. Additionally, the limited access to water for basic needs has severe implications for public health, hygiene, and overall quality of life.ltbrgtGRRN aims to address critical WASH needs in Dinsor district by providing life-saving interventions for 2,500 rural households (15,000 individuals). The project focuses on rehabilitating essential water infrastructure, including six (6) shallow wells contaminated by El Niño floods. Water quality will be ensured through inspections, sampling, testing, and treatment. These water points will be managed collaboratively by the community, local authorities, and a gender-balanced water management committee trained in operations and maintenance. GRRN also plans to construct 125 emergency latrines, 15% of which will be disability-friendly and equipped with solar lamps to enhance safety. Provision of 125 sanitation tool kits and will conduct 21 solid waste management campaigns, Hygiene promotion will be prioritized with 48 sessions and the purchase and distribution of 1,250 hygiene kits. GRRN follows SPHERE standards and Somalia WASH cluster guidelines, integrating gender and disability considerations, in alignment with IASC recommendations for GBV interventions. The initiative emphasizes community engagement and cross-sectoral collaboration with partners like Save the Children, ACF, and to meet both immediate and long-term needs, fostering sustainable operations through local partnerships. ltbrgtGRRN’s plan to integrate the SHF WASH project with MARDO’s nutrition program in key areas such as Sinai village, Balila1, Balila2, Rami Dhaw, and Yaqshid village is a strategic approach to maximize the impact on targeted communities, especially within IDP and rural settings. The additional coordination with partners like GREDO, Save the Children, MARDO, and WARDO will reinforce complementarity and alignment among the various health, nutrition, livelihood, and protection interventions, ensuring a well-rounded, efficient response and reducing the risk of overlapping efforts. This integrated strategy should significantly enhance the resilience and overall well-being of the communities served.lt/pgt
